context:
Goal: a restore on the phone stays restored after the next sync.
Problem (risk): the web gives every restored key the restore time (restampRestore in src/merge-rules.mjs), but the native app keeps the old times. So a later Worker reply can undo part of a phone restore. The fix needs your choice, because the native build keeps the merge rules out of its bundle.
Based on (read): debt native-restore-keeps-old-times.
Based on (read): the native pull reached the live Worker (PR #185).
Departs from: build.mjs:RULES_OUT — the merge rules stay out of native rules.js; option a bundles restampRestore into it.
Meanwhile: pins works on its other debts. Nothing waits on this.

options.gain: The phone restores exactly like the web, from one shared rule.
options.how: The native rules.js gains the web's restampRestore, and the phone calls it on every restore.
options.label: Bundle restampRestore into the phone's rules
options.lose: The phone's rules bundle grows by the merge rules file.

options.gain: The bundle stays as it is.
options.how: A Swift copy of the rule restamps each restored key.
options.label: Rewrite restampRestore in Swift
options.lose: Two copies of one rule, which can drift apart.

options.how: No app change now. Lane W3b, which is blocked, makes the Worker restamp.
options.label: Leave it until the Worker restamps
options.lose: A phone restore can be partly undone in the meantime.

ref: debt native-restore-keeps-old-times (a phone restore keeps the old times); decision a-restore-is-not-local (a restore is not a local edit); PR #185 (the native pull reached the live Worker)
title: A restore on the phone keeps the old times, so a sync can undo part of it. How should the phone restamp?
why: It is the only option that keeps one home for the rule and closes the gap now.
